    Markdown¶

    rn_forge.commons.text.markdown ¶

    Markdown structure: headings, anchors, links, tables and fenced code.

    Documents are parsed with markdown-it-py (CommonMark plus GFM tables). Heading anchors follow Python-Markdown's toc extension, which MkDocs uses.

    MarkdownHeading(level, text, anchor, line) dataclass ¶

    A heading of a Markdown document.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    level int

    The heading level, 1 to 6.
    text str

    The heading as plain text; inline markup is dropped and code spans are kept as text.
    anchor str

    The anchor a renderer gives the heading, unique within the document.
    line int

    The 0-based line of the heading.

    MarkdownTable(header, rows, start, end) dataclass ¶

    A GFM pipe table of a Markdown document.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    header tuple[str, ...]

    The header cells.
    rows tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]

    The body rows, each exactly len(header) cells.
    start int

    The 0-based line of the header row.
    end int

    The 0-based line after the last row.

    MarkdownUtils ¶

    Read the structure of Markdown text.

    anchors(text) staticmethod ¶

    Return the anchors of the headings of text.

    headings(text) staticmethod ¶

    List the ATX and setext headings of text, in document order.

    A heading inside code is not listed. A repeated anchor gets _1, _2 and so on.

    is_external(link) staticmethod ¶

    Return whether link has a URL scheme or is scheme-relative.

    links(text) staticmethod ¶

    List the link and image targets of text, in document order.

    Inline, reference, collapsed-reference and autolink targets are included, percent-decoded. A reference with no definition and anything inside code is not a link.

    Example::

    MarkdownUtils.links("[a](b%20c.md) ![i](p.png)")  # ["b c.md", "p.png"]

    slugify(text, separator='-') staticmethod ¶

    Return the anchor slug of text, as Python-Markdown's toc makes it.

    Example::

    MarkdownUtils.slugify("Hello, World!")  # "hello-world"

    strip_fenced_code(text) staticmethod ¶

    Return text with every line of every fenced code block removed.

    tables(text) staticmethod ¶

    List the GFM pipe tables of text, in document order.

    A table inside code is not listed. Cells are stripped; a short row is padded with empty cells to the header's width.

    title(text) staticmethod ¶

    Return the text of the first level-1 heading, or None.

    Made with Material for MkDocs
